How do I structure a large React project?

Feature-based structure scales better than type-based.

```
src/
├── features/             # Group by feature
│   ├── auth/
│   │   ├── components/   # LoginForm, RegisterForm
│   │   ├── hooks/        # useAuth, useLogin
│   │   ├── api.ts        # login(), register()
│   │   └── index.ts      # Public exports
│   ├── dashboard/
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   ├── hooks/
│   │   └── api.ts
│   └── settings/
├── shared/               # Cross-feature code
│   ├── components/       # Button, Input, Modal
│   ├── hooks/            # useDebounce, usePrevious
│   ├── utils/            # formatDate, cn()
│   └── types.ts          # Global types
├── app/                  # App setup
│   ├── routes.tsx
│   └── providers.tsx
└── config/               # Constants, env vars
```

**Rules:**
- Each feature is self-contained (components + hooks + API)
- Features import from `shared/`, never from other features
- `index.ts` exports only the public API of each feature
- Deleting a feature = deleting one folder

This scales to 50+ developers because teams own features independently, reducing merge conflicts and coupling.
